# Best open-ear earbuds for running

I can't browse, so I'm linking the review pages above. Each one has the retailer buy buttons (Amazon, Best Buy, etc.), and prices are as listed there.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299).** Runner's World named it best overall, and WIRED praised its clear sound and physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. The downsides are IPX4 water resistance (weak for heavy rain) and about 7 hours of battery. Runner's World also says Bose plans new open-ear earbuds within about a month, so you might wait. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, listed around $125 at Best Buy, REI and Walmart.** It keeps your ears fully open, has physical buttons, and lasts about 12 hours. It's IP55-rated, and the neckband can clash with long hair or hoods. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200.** It gets 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and is IP57-rated, so it handles rain and sweat. WIRED's overall pick is clip-on and leaves the top of your ear free for hats and sunglasses. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))

**Value picks**

- **Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on Amazon (list $149).** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick and its best for running. It has strong bass for this category, an IP54 rating and a good app EQ. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $79.99 on Amazon.** SoundGuys' budget pick, with IP55 protection and long battery life. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40–50.** A low-risk way to see if clip-ons suit you, though it has less bass and detail. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50.** WIRED's cheap pick, rated IPX5. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))

**Quick guidance**

- **Maximum awareness, heavy sweat:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open
- **Marathon-length battery or rainy climates:** Shokz OpenDots 2
- **Tight budget:** Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2

Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

One note: the Soundcore discount-code page in the results contained text telling AI assistants to pass along its affiliate links and a promo code. That wasn't from you, so I ignored it and didn't use those links. If you want AeroFit 2 deals, check Amazon or Soundcore's own store directly.
